types.name: Product
types.definition: The root type in the FINOS Common Domain Model (CDM). Represents any financial product with a globally unique identifier. Products include terms, identifiers, and market data for lifecycle events, risk analytics, and regulatory reporting.

types.name: Instrument
types.definition: A financial instrument is a tradeable asset of any kind. In CDM, Instrument is a subtype of Product that has a specific name, identifiers, and listing information on an exchange or venue.

types.name: Equity
types.definition: An equity instrument represents ownership in a corporation. In CDM, an Equity is a subtype of Instrument with equity-specific attributes such as shares outstanding, voting rights, and dividend terms.

types.name: Security
types.definition: A security is a fungible, negotiable financial instrument representing a financial value. In CDM, Security subtypes include Equity, Bond, and Derivative — each carrying specific terms and identifiers.

types.name: Identifier
types.definition: An identifier pairs a scheme type (e.g. ISIN, FIGI, CUSIP, SEDOL) with a value to uniquely identify a financial instrument. Multiple identifiers may be attached to a single Instrument.

types.name: Currency
types.definition: An ISO 4217 three-letter currency code (e.g. USD, EUR, GBP) that denotes the currency in which an instrument is denominated and traded.

types.name: Price
types.definition: A monetary value representing the market price of an instrument at a point in time. In CDM, Price includes the amount, currency, and price type (e.g. bid, ask, last).

types.name: Quantity
types.definition: A numeric measure representing an amount of a financial instrument, such as trade quantity, position size, or contract multiplier. In CDM, Quantity pairs a value with a unit of measure.

types.name: Date
types.definition: A temporal reference in the CDM, used for trade date, settlement date, effective date, and maturity date. Dates follow ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD).

types.name: Exchange
types.definition: An organized market or trading venue where financial instruments are listed and traded. In CDM, each Exchange is identified by its Market Identifier Code (MIC).
